audit.whatIsWrong: Three sources give three different level charts and I could not reconcile them safely. The urgot page reads Urgot/Urgot/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill; the packet chart reads Urgot x6 then Mordekaiser; the mirror (mordekaiser__urgot) reports Skill/Mordekaiser/Mordekaiser/Skill/Mordekaiser/Urgot/Urgot.
audit.why: The mirror chart hands Mordekaiser levels 2, 3 and 6 and hands Urgot both item rows — the opposite shape to the packet and to both prose layers here, which say Urgot wins early short trades and the lane flips once Realm of Death and AP items are online at 54.75% for Urgot.
audit.corrected: LEFT UNCHANGED and raised as a question rather than guessed. Proposing either shape would either contradict the packet or fight the mirror, and a half-right chart ships two answers to a paying user.

audit.why: Four spikes keyed to Lvl 3-5, Lvl 6 (Realm of Death), 1st item and Late — matches the real curve, and the mirror agrees no spike change is needed.
audit.corrected: Only spikes[2].text needed the anti-heal timing added.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers anywhere, and breakdown.cooldowns describes Death's Grasp as carrying 'passive magic pen' with no timing. Separately, the kit file flags Obliterate (Q) as grounding.
audit.why: DERIVED-FLAG MISFIRE confirmed by the mirror: Riot's description of Obliterate is only 'smashes the ground with his mace dealing damage... damage is increased when hitting a single enemy'. There is no grounding in that text, so I wrote nothing claiming Obliterate denies Disdain (E). Per the rule, the description wins over the flag. The real numbers that matter: Obliterate 8s at rank 1 falling to 4s at rank 5, Death's Grasp 16s falling to 8s, Indestructible 12s, Realm of Death 140s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Trade in the window right after Obliterate and the Death's Grasp pull are spent; Realm of Death is 140s at rank 1, so poking him under the Fear Beyond Death threshold makes casting it a losing bet for him.

audit.whatIsWrong: Indestructible (W) converts stored damage into a heal on a 12s cooldown, and nothing in the lane text keyed Grievous Wounds to it.
audit.why: Extended trades are decided by whether that heal lands at full value; report[8] already buys Executioner's Calling first back but no prose explained why.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds before Black Cleaver blunts the Indestructible heal — now stated in spikes[2].text and whys[5].

edits.before: - Mordekaiser Realm of Death: matchup-defining — His 1v1 realm. Poke him low before he uses it. Track it before every engage. - Mordekaiser Death’s Grasp: Pulls enemies toward him after a delay + passive magic pen. Dodge or sidestep it.
edits.after: - Realm of Death (R), 140s at rank 1: his 1v1 realm — poke him under 25% before he casts it. - Obliterate (Q) is 8s at rank 1 and 4s at rank 5, Death's Grasp (E) 16s down to 8s — step in right after the pull whiffs.

edits.before: Black Cleaver keeps your Purge shred ahead of his Indestructible healing in short trades, but avoid extended fights where his passive and E (Death's Grasp) pull let him ramp damage.
edits.after: Indestructible (W) heals off stored damage every 12s, so Executioner's Calling before Cleaver blunts it. Keep trades short — his passive and the Death's Grasp (E) pull are what ramp his damage.

edits.before: First item your Purge shred stays ahead of his Indestructible healing.
edits.after: First item, Grievous Wounds keeps his Indestructible heal small.

edits.before: Land Q (Obliterate) and stack Indestructible (W) shield
edits.after: Land Obliterate (Q) off cooldown to stack his W shield

edits.before: His 1v1 realm. Poke him low before he uses it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: His 1v1 realm, 140s at rank 1. Poke him under 25% first — then he cannot afford to cast it.

notes: I did not touch the level chart: packet, page and mirror all disagree in different directions (see audit point 2) and a partial chart edit blocks the whole champion in regression-check. Kit-generator bug worth fixing: Mordekaiser's Obliterate (Q) carries a grounding flag that Riot's description does not support — the same misfire would tell every dash champion in the game that Morde's Q denies their mobility.
